# Allowed entries by context
#
# Polars: the release py-2.2.0 at the commit 08b2814ce6386c0efe0fea512912353f42a8b7b6 of vendor/polars.
# Generated from the catalogue and Polars by the engine test
# `allowed::tests::artifacts::the_committed_tables_are_what_polars_gives`, with Polars on
# one thread, so that a reason that depends on which of two failures comes first is the
# same every time, in the Cargo profile `measure`, which builds Polars as its release
# does: optimised, without debug assertions or overflow checks. Do not edit.
# To refresh after a change of the catalogue or of Polars:
#   DAGEIST_REFRESH_TABLES=1 cargo test --offline --locked --profile measure -p dageist-engine \
#     allowed::tests::artifacts
# See docs/how-to.md, "Refresh The Tables Of Allowed Combinations".
#
# Each line is: entry | context | chain | receiver | argument | rules | outcome.
#
# An entry that is not a step stands in a context: a position of a step that holds an
# expression, such as `select`, or such a position inside another expression, such as
# `select > over.order_by`. Each entry in each context has two lines, one for each chain:
#
#   continues: the chain goes on from the entry, with the neutral continuation the context
#     needs, and the line says whether the entry may stand there at all. The continuation
#     is `.is_not_null()` where a `Boolean` is required (a filter's predicate, what a
#     condition gives in a filter, a condition's predicate), a cast to the dtype of the
#     other table's key (`Int64`) for the whole expression in a join key, `.first()`
#     for the whole expression in a pivot's aggregate, and `.is_not_null().all()` for the
#     whole expression in a `having`. Where the context needs nothing,
#     nothing follows. Polars refusing the entry however it goes on, as it refuses a window
#     in a join key, makes the entry unable to stand.
#   ends: the chain ends at the entry as it is, and the line says whether the entry may end
#     an expression there. A `Boolean` is required of a chain that ends in a filter, so an
#     entry that gives something else may stand there, followed by what makes a `Boolean`,
#     though it may not end the chain.
#
# A method is measured on the receiver and argument dtypes that fit it best, the first
# that runs in the dtype table (`Int64` first), and, where the chain ends in a context that
# needs a `Boolean`, one that gives a `Boolean` if there is one. A method that takes an
# option in place of a parameter, as a fill takes a strategy in place of a value, has the
# lines of each word of it besides, the entry written with the form, such as
# `Expr.fill_null[strategy=forward]`, for Polars calls a fill by `zero` elementwise and by
# `forward` not. `drop_nulls` and `drop_nans` are measured on a column with no null, for
# how many values a column that holds one gives is for the rows to say. The result of an allowed
# method is what it gives on its own. `col` and `lit` are measured, where the chain ends and
# a `Boolean` is needed, on a `Boolean` column and literal, and on a column of whole numbers
# and the literal `1` otherwise. Where the chain ends in a join key, the other table's key
# has the dtype the key has. `join_right` is evaluated against the other table, whose
# columns are named differently from the left table's; `pivot_aggregate` starts from
# `element()`, and a method's arguments there are nulls of their dtype. `group_key`,
# `aggregate` and `having` are the keys of `group_by` on the column `k`, the aggregates of
# `agg` and the predicates of `having`, the last two evaluated on the rows of each group: an
# entry that aggregates gives one value for each group, and `many` there is a list of values
# for each group, of the dtype the line gives. A `having` needs one value for each group.
#
# The rules column names the rules that govern the line, which dageist holds and Polars
# does not. The outcome is Polars' alone, whatever the rules say. The rules are:
#   arrays-meet-at-one-width: arrays that meet, as the operands of a method or the values of a condition, and give an array, or that one is looked up in, must be of one width, which must be known: Polars refuses to add arrays of two widths or to look one up in the other, and gives a list where it fills one with the other or takes one for a value of a condition and the other for another.
#   condition-predicate-is-boolean: a condition's predicate must be Boolean.
#   duration-is-valid: a duration typed in must be a duration string Polars reads.
#   element-dtype-is-implemented: a method of lists and arrays must be given an element dtype that Polars implements it for: it panics for the others where the rows run, on a thread of its own that its streaming executor may not recover from.
#   element-dtype-is-measured: a method whose answer depends on the element dtype of a list or an array must be given one the tables measure it on, the whole numbers, the floats, text, booleans, dates and datetimes: Polars is not asked of another, which it may panic on.
#   element-only-in-pivot-aggregate: `polars.element` stands only in a pivot's aggregate.
#   field-is-of-the-struct: a field that a method reads or drops must be one of the fields of the struct it follows: Polars refuses a name that is none, as one that was renamed or dropped before is.
#   field-names-fit-the-struct: the names given to the fields of a struct must be as many as its fields where it is renamed, or as the places of the array it is made of, and no two fields of a struct may be named alike: Polars refuses names of another number and two fields of one name.
#   filter-predicate-is-boolean: a filter's predicate must be Boolean.
#   folded-function-is-no-join-key: a moment or a length of time made of numbers typed in is folded by Polars into a literal named by an alias, which a join's key may not hold: give it a column among its parts, or make it in a step before the join.
#   grouped-names-are-distinct: the columns a group by gives must be named differently: a key is named by the column it reads or the name it is given, an aggregate by the column its chain reads or the name it is given, and Polars refuses two that are named alike, as a key and an aggregate of the same column are.
#   having-casts-to-boolean: a having's predicate must be a value Polars casts to a Boolean to keep a group or not: a Boolean, a number, or null where it stands alone, and not text, a date, a list or a struct, which it refuses when it runs the rows; beside another predicate, which Polars combines it with as the predicates of a filter are, it must be a Boolean.
#   having-gives-one-value: a having's predicate must give one value for each group: the values of the group, as a column or a method that keeps some of them gives, are a list that Polars cannot cast to a Boolean when it runs the rows, so give an aggregate such as the sum, the first value, whether all are true, or a count compared with a number.
#   is-in-takes-a-list: is_in must be given a list or an array to look the value up in, or a collection imploded, and not a collection nested as deeply as the value it follows, as a column of its own dtype is: Polars deprecates that form as ambiguous (pola-rs/polars#22149) and panics on one value looked up in another, so give a list, or the collection imploded.
#   join-key-names-are-not-repeated: a join may not pair the same two output column names twice: where two keys on one side are named alike, the keys they are paired with must be named differently.
#   kept-order-needs-keys-of-the-rows: where `maintain_order` keeps the order of the groups, a key must give one value or as many as the table has rows: Polars refuses a key that takes some of the values, as head, filter and drop_nulls do, for lengths that differ where the arguments or the data make it fewer, so give the key as a column, or leave the order unset.
#   key-is-elementwise: a join's key, and the key of a window in what a group by evaluates in `agg` or `having`, must be elementwise: an aggregate may not stand in it beside a column, nor a method that takes some of the values, as head and filter do, unless it goes on to an aggregate, nor a column be compared with a null, nor a column of whole numbers be compared for missing values with a literal that is a number with a fraction or a whole number its dtype cannot hold, as Polars reads the literal (a literal of 16 bit floats or of Boolean, and a float that does not cast exactly, are kept), nor a replacement take a value that reads a column.
#   literal-beside-values-in-a-group: in `agg` and `having`, a literal that dt.replace, str.splitn or str.split_exact maps may not be given the values of the group beside it (in a `having` only where it stands beside another value), nor one value that an aggregate gave in a `having`, a literal that sort_by sorts by them may not stand alone, and a literal that replace, replace_strict, str.replace or str.replace_all replaces may not be given either: Polars cannot replace a literal by values for each row, and refuses the map of one value beside many as of another length.
#   moments-share-a-zone: moments that are compared, subtracted, filled, bound by one another, or given as the values of a condition or as a replacement's new values and default, must be in one time zone: Polars finds no dtype that two zones have in common, and fails where a shift is filled with a moment of another zone.
#   one-column-is-needed: a filter's only predicate must be one column: an expression that gives several, as the unnest of a struct of several fields does, is ambiguous, and one that gives none, as the unnest of a struct of no field does, is empty, and Polars refuses both; beside another predicate each expression it expands to is a predicate of its own, which it takes.
#   parameter-takes-one-value: a parameter that Polars reads as one value must be given one: not the rows, nor a count of values that the data or the arguments decide, and, for the count of rows that `shift` and `diff` look back by and the value `shift` fills with, not the one value that a method took of one value either, which Polars cannot tell is one before the rows run.
#   pattern-is-valid: a pattern must be a valid regular expression.
#   pivot-aggregate-gives-one-value: a pivot's aggregate must give one value for each group.
#   range-is-valid: a range or a repeat typed in must be one Polars can make and cut: a step other than nothing, an interval above nothing that its bounds are read in, bounds the dtype holds, a number of values that is not below nothing, and, of it, no length below nothing to cut any value by.
#   replacement-values-match-in-number: a replacement takes as many new values as old ones, or one, and a strict one a default of as many values as what it follows, or one.
#   struct-arithmetic-needs-numbers: arithmetic with a struct needs its fields to be numbers: Polars refuses the absolute value, the negation, the sign, a clip and a power of a struct whatever its fields are, and the sum, the difference, the product and the quotients of one that has a field of text, a date, a moment or a time.
#   struct-is-filled-forward-or-backward: a struct is filled by a strategy only forward or backward: Polars refuses the smallest, the largest, the mean, zero and one where the struct holds a null, which a pivot's missing cells make, and does nothing where it holds none.
#   time-zone-is-valid: a time zone must be one Polars reads.
#   to-struct-names-are-distinct: no two names given to the fields of a struct that a list or an array is made may be alike: Polars 2.2.0 accepts them and builds a struct that disagrees with itself, as its dtype and its series hold two fields of one name, and refuses the same names for a struct made of columns or renamed.
#   values-meet-in-count: the values a call meets must be one value, which meets each of the others, or as many as one another: a count of values that the data or the arguments decide, as the first values of a column or the values that differ are, is not the table's rows and not another count it is not known to equal.
#   window-input-is-not-counted: a window takes a value as long as its group, and a count of values that the data or the arguments decide is not, nor is the one value that a method took of one value, unless the window joins the values of a group into a list or explodes them.
#   window-input-is-not-widened: a window takes a value as long as its input, and a value of one row that a part widens, as dt.replace's parts do, is not: Polars refuses the length of its output.
#   written-names-are-distinct: the columns that the items of a select or of with_columns write must be named differently: an unnest and a field read write the names of the fields, and Polars refuses two items that write one name.
#
# An outcome is `allowed <dtype of the result> <one|many>` (`-` for a step), or
# `refused <stage>: <Polars' reason>`. A combination is allowed only when Polars resolved
# its schema, ran it on three rows that include a null, and ran it on a table with no rows.
# The stage is where Polars refused it: `schema`; `rows`, when the schema resolved and
# the rows were refused; or `empty`, when only the table with no rows was. `one` is a
# value for the three rows together, `many` any other number. A reason is Polars' message
# up to its first blank line, on one line.
#
# 25830 combinations: 18164 allowed; 3278 refused when Polars resolved the schema, 4388 when it ran the rows, 0 when it ran the empty table.
#
